tools.name: app_tool_box
tools.description: Internal helper for GitKraken MCP apps. App-only — agents must not call this tool.

action.description: App helper action to execute. Supported values: 'git_status_data', 'git_graph_data', 'git_graph_commit_changes', 'git_graph_targets', 'compose_history', 'git_status_line_changes', 'open_diff', 'open_file', 'open_in_explorer', 'detected_editors', 'git_push', 'git_pull', 'git_fetch', 'git_add_or_commit', 'git_generate_commit_message', 'git_stash', 'app_feedback', 'gitlens_ping', 'gitlens_open_graph', 'update_user_preferences', 'interaction_telemetry', 'user_status', 'save_auth_code', 'purchase_url', 'start_trial', 'resend_email', 'ai_models_list', 'ai_model_set', 'settings_snapshot', 'settings_account_url', 'settings_organizations', 'settings_set_organization', 'compose_plan', 'compose_plan_start', 'compose_plan_status', 'compose_plan_cancel', 'compose_open_diff', 'compose_apply_plan', 'git_resolve_data', 'git_resolve_prepare_start', 'git_resolve_prepare_status', 'git_resolve_prepare_cancel', 'git_resolve_file_retry', 'git_resolve_file_open_diff', 'git_resolve_apply', 'git_resolve_discard'.

options.description: Per-action options. Supported keys depend on the 'action' value and include 'app_name', 'base_remote_url', 'base_sha', 'code', 'comment', 'commit_id', 'commit_sha', 'context', 'cursor', 'custom_instructions', 'data', 'description', 'direction', 'editor_id', 'file_allow_list', 'file_path', 'files', 'files_json', 'focused_file_paths', 'force', 'git_action', 'git_commit_composer_app_collapsed', 'git_graph_app_collapsed', 'git_status_app_collapsed', 'guidance', 'head_remote_url', 'head_sha', 'include_untracked', 'instructions', 'interaction', 'issue_url', 'job_id', 'launchpad_issue_filters', 'launchpad_pr_filters', 'launchpad_stale_threshold_days', 'launchpad_view', 'message', 'organization_id', 'page', 'plan_json', 'pr_number', 'pr_url', 'provider', 'providers', 'range_start_sha', 'refresh', 'sentiment', 'session_id', 'source_type', 'staged_only', and 'target_branch'.

tools.name: app_update_user_preferences
tools.description: Update GitKraken CLI user preferences for MCP apps. App-only; agents must not call this tool.

git_commit_composer_app_collapsed.description: When true, future Git Commit Composer overview app loads start in the collapsed state.

git_graph_app_collapsed.description: When true, future Git Graph overview app loads start in the collapsed state.

git_status_app_collapsed.description: When true, future Git Status overview app loads start in the collapsed state.

launchpad_issue_filters.description: Serialized issue filter selections for Launchpad.

launchpad_pr_filters.description: Serialized pull request filter selections for Launchpad.

launchpad_stale_threshold_days.description: Number of days of inactivity after which a Launchpad pull request is treated as stale and de-prioritized.

launchpad_view.description: Selected Launchpad view: pull-requests, issues, or all.

tools.name: git_add
tools.description: Add file contents to the index (git add <pathspec>).

directory.description: The directory to run git add in

files.description: Optional array of files to add. If omitted, all files are added.

tools.name: git_blame
tools.description: Show what revision and author last modified each line of a file (git blame <file>).

directory.description: The directory to run git blame in

tools.name: git_branch
tools.description: List or create branches (git branch).

action.description: Git branch action to be executed

branch_name.description: (Optional) Name of the branch to create or delete

directory.description: The directory to run git branch in

tools.name: git_checkout
tools.description: Switch branches or restore working tree files (git checkout <branch>).

branch.description: The branch to checkout. This must be a valid branch name without spaces

directory.description: The directory to run git checkout in

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: Record changes to the repository (git commit -m <message> [files...]).

directory.description: The directory to run git commit in

files.description: Optional array of files to commit. If omitted, all staged changes are committed.

tools.name: git_commit_composer
tools.description: Show the commit composer for a repository, will open a UI if client supports it.

custom_instructions.description: Free-form guidance for the AI commit composer. Only meaningful when 'direction' is 'custom'.

direction.description: Initial grouping preset for the composer. 'auto' lets the AI choose; 'area' groups by codebase area / subsystem; 'type' groups by conventional commit type; 'custom' uses the supplied 'custom_instructions' text. Defaults to 'auto'.

tools.name: git_fetch
tools.description: Download objects and refs from another repository (git fetch).

directory.description: The directory to run git fetch in

tools.name: git_graph
tools.description: Show the commit graph for a repository (git log --graph), will open a UI if client supports it.

tools.name: git_log_or_diff
tools.description: Show commit logs or changes between commits (git log --oneline or git diff).

action.description: The action to perform: 'log' for commit logs or 'diff' for changes

authors.description: Optional array of author names or emails to filter commits by (only applies to 'log' action)

directory.description: The directory to run the command in

revision_range.description: Optional revision range (e.g., 'HEAD', 'main..feature', 'abc123', 'HEAD~5..HEAD'). For 'diff' action, shows differences for the specified range. For 'log' action, shows commits in the range. Defaults to HEAD.

since.description: Optional date/timestamp/relative time to show commits after (e.g., '2024-01-01', '2 weeks ago', 'yesterday', '1 hour ago', '3 days ago'). Only applies to 'log' action.

until.description: Optional date/timestamp/relative time to show commits before (e.g., '2024-12-31', '1 week ago', 'today', 'yesterday', '2 hours ago'). Only applies to 'log' action.

tools.name: git_pull
tools.description: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch (git pull).

directory.description: The directory to run git pull in

tools.name: git_push
tools.description: Update remote refs along with associated objects (git push).

directory.description: The directory to run git push in

tools.name: git_resolve
tools.description: Show the conflict resolution UI for a repository, will open a UI if client supports it.

instructions.description: Optional guidance for the AI conflict resolution flow.

tools.name: git_stash
tools.description: Stash the changes in a dirty working directory (git stash).

directory.description: The directory to run git stash in

include_untracked.description: When true, include untracked files in the stash.

name.description: Optional name for the stash (used as the stash message)

staged_only.description: When true, stash only the currently staged changes and leave unstaged work untouched.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Show the working tree status (git status), will open a UI if client supports it.

tools.name: git_worktree
tools.description: List or add git worktrees (git worktree <action>).

action.description: Git worktree action to be executed

branch.description: (Optional) Existing branch for the new worktree (used for add)

directory.description: The directory to run git worktree in

path.description: (Optional) Path for the worktree (required for add)

tools.name: gitkraken_workspace_list
tools.description: Lists all Gitkraken workspaces

tools.name: gitlens_launchpad
tools.description: Gitlens Launchpad. Gets your open pull requests prioritized by what needs attention: ready to merge, has conflicts, awaiting review, etc. Helpful for checking todos, outstanding tasks, or deciding what to work on next.

tools.name: gitlens_start_review
tools.description: Gitlens Start Review. Creates a dedicated worktree and reviews your PR with an AI agent.

instructions.description: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about the review focus, review criteria, or what aspects to check. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions. Examples: 'focus on security issues', 'check for performance regressions', 'review only the authentication logic'.

pr_url.description: URL of the PR to start review.

tools.name: gitlens_start_work
tools.description: Gitlens Start Work. Creates a work based on an issue. This tool will create a branch and link it with the issue, keeping context visible throughout your work.

instructions.description: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about the implementation approach, or additional context to supplement the issue. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions.

issue_url.description: URL of the issue to start work on.

tools.name: issues_add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an issue

azure_organization.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

comment.description: The text content of the comment (markdown; converted to Jira's format for Jira. Azure DevOps expects HTML)

issue_id.description: The ID of the issue to comment on

provider.description: Specify the issue provider. Default is JIRA

repository_name.description: Repository name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

repository_organization.description: Organization name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

tools.name: issues_assigned_to_me
tools.description: Fetch issues assigned to the user. Set assigned_to_me=false to broaden the result to all visible issues. To filter server-side by assignee, set unassigned=true for issues with no assignee, or assigned_to=<user> for issues assigned to a specific person (assigned_to_me, unassigned and assigned_to are mutually exclusive). Narrow results further with repository_name/repository_organization (GitHub), project/issue_type (Jira), or is_closed.

assigned_to.description: List only issues assigned to this user (username/email/accountId, provider-dependent). Mutually exclusive with assigned_to_me and unassigned. Not supported by Trello/Linear.

assigned_to_me.description: Whether to limit results to issues assigned to you. Defaults to true.

azure_organization.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

fields.description: Optional comma-separated list of top-level fields to keep on each result. Recommended for list/overview calls: omitting it returns every field, which on large lists can overflow the context window. Omit only when you need the full objects. If every requested name is unknown, the request is rejected; field names are case-sensitive. Available fields: id, url, number, provider, repoName, repoOwner, repoHost, project, title, description, issueType, status, updatedAt, assignees, comments, childIssues.

is_closed.description: Set to true to return closed/done issues instead of open issues. Defaults to false.

issue_type.description: Issue type. Jira only (e.g. Bug, Story, Task).

page.description: Optional parameter to specify the page number, defaults to 1

provider.description: Specify the issue provider. Default is JIRA

repository_name.description: Repository name. GitHub only; must be combined with repository_organization.

unassigned.description: Set to true to list only unassigned issues. Mutually exclusive with assigned_to_me and assigned_to. Not supported by Trello.

tools.name: issues_create
tools.description: Create a new issue. For Jira, repository_name is the project key. For Linear, repository_organization is the team UUID, key, or name.

assignees.description: Optional list of assignees. GitHub: usernames; GitLab: user IDs; Jira/Linear/Azure: first entry is used

azure_organization.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

body.description: The body/description of the issue (markdown; converted to Jira's format for Jira. Azure DevOps expects HTML)

issue_type.description: Issue type. Jira only (e.g. Bug, Story, Task); defaults to Task.

labels.description: Optional list of label names to apply

provider.description: Specify the issue provider. Default is JIRA

repository_name.description: Repository name. Required for GitHub/GitLab; required for Jira, where it is the project key (e.g. GKCLI)

repository_organization.description: Organization name. Required for GitHub/GitLab; for Linear use as team identifier

tools.name: issues_get_detail
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific issue by its unique ID. For Jira Epics, the response includes a childIssues array containing all issues linked to the epic.

azure_organization.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

issue_id.description: The Number or ID of the issue to retrieve. Supported formats include GitHub/GitLab numeric IDs (e.g., 123 or #123), Jira keys (e.g., PROJ-123), Linear issue IDs (UUID format), etc.

provider.description: Specify the issue provider. Default is JIRA

repository_name.description: Repository name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

repository_organization.description: Organization name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

tools.name: pull_request_assigned_to_me
tools.description: Search pull requests where you are the author or assignee. Set reviewer to true to also include pull requests where you are a requested reviewer (github and gitlab only).

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

fields.description: Optional comma-separated list of top-level fields to keep on each result. Recommended for list/overview calls: omitting it returns every field, which on large lists can overflow the context window. Omit only when you need the full objects. If every requested name is unknown, the request is rejected; field names are case-sensitive. Available fields: timestampCreatedAt, updatedAt, mergedAt, closedAt, title, description, url, state, owner, repoName, repoHost, provider, id, nodeId, repositoryId, projectId, organization, files, clone, number, merged, draft, approved, authoredByMe, headBranch, baseBranch, headRepo, author, assignees, reviews, reviewDecision, mergeableState, buildStatuses, baseRef, headRef, additions, deletions, changedFiles, filesTruncated, currentViewer.

is_closed.description: Set to true if you want to search for closed pull requests

page.description: Optional parameter to specify the page number, defaults to 1

repository_name.description: Set the repository name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

repository_organization.description: Set the organization name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

reviewer.description: Set to true to also include pull requests where you are a requested reviewer. Supported by github, github_enterprise, gitlab, gitlab_self_hosted; ignored for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket.

with_branches.description: Include head/base branch names on each result. For GitHub this triggers an extra API call per PR, so leave off unless branches are needed.

assign_to_me.description: Assign the newly created pull request to the current authenticated user when supported by the provider

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

body.description: The body/description of the pull request

repository_name.description: Set the repository name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

repository_organization.description: Set the organization name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

source_branch.description: Source branch from which the pull request will be created

target_branch.description: Target branch where the pull request will be merged

title.description: The title of the pull request

tools.description: Create a review for a pull request

approve.description: Set to true if you want to approve the pull request

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

pull_request_id.description: ID of the pull request to create the review for

repository_name.description: Set the repository name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

repository_organization.description: Set the organization name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

review.description: Comment to add to the pull request review

tools.name: pull_request_get_comments
tools.description: Get all the comments in a pull requests

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

pull_request_id.description: ID of the pull request to add the comment to

repository_name.description: Set the repository name of the pull request

repository_organization.description: Set the organization name of the pull request

tools.name: pull_request_get_detail
tools.description: Get an specific pull request

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

pull_request_files.description: Set to true if you want to retrieve the files changed in the pull request. Not supported by Azure DevOps. On GitHub and GitLab the list is paged past the provider's first page. `changedFiles` is the provider-reported total where the provider supplies one; it is absent otherwise, and Bitbucket never supplies it. `filesTruncated` is true when the returned list is known to be short and absent otherwise; Bitbucket Cloud never sets it because that provider gives no completeness signal. `diffOmitted` on a file means its patch, blob sha and urls were elided to bound the response size. `additions`, `deletions` and `changes` are populated on GitHub only. The `files` key is null, not absent, when this parameter is not set.

pull_request_id.description: ID of the pull request to retrieve

repository_name.description: Set the repository name of the pull request

repository_organization.description: Set the organization name of the pull request

tools.description: Get file content from a repository

azure_project.description: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

file_path.description: File path to retrieve from the repository

ref.description: Set the branch, tag, or commit SHA to retrieve the file from

repository_organization.description: Set the organization name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket
